newsitem.title: USA: Jury deliberates reputed mobster case in New York.
newsitem.headline: Jury deliberates reputed mobster case in New York.

text.p: A federal jury on Wednesday began deliberating charges of murder and racketeering against accused New York City mob boss Vincent "The Chin" Gigante.
U.S. District Judge Jack Weinstein gave the jurors nearly two hours of instructions before they began deliberations.
The jury has heard testimony from six mob informants and a dozen law enforcement agents during almost four weeks in Brooklyn federal court.
Gigante, the reputed head of the Genovese crime family, faces a 21-count indictment. He is accused of ordering seven murders, plotting to kill three other people, rigging business bids and extortion.

Gigante's defence attorneys say he is incapacitated by mental illness. He earned the nickname "The Oddfather" for his habit of wandering the neighbourhood around his Greenwich Village apartment in a tattered bathrobe.
But prosecutors say Gigante has feigned illness for years to avoid prosecution.
The government called a string of mobsters who turned informants to testify against Gigante, reputed to be one of New York City's last old-time dons.

Among the informants was Salvatore "Sammy the Bull" Gravano, whose testimony was key in the 1992 murder and racketeering conviction of Gambino godfather John Gotti. Gotti is serving life in prison without the possibility of parole.

Gigante's defence attorneys have argued the informants were witnesses willing to modify their testimony to suit the government. They also argued that Anthony "Fat Tony" Salerno was convicted of being the Genovese crime family boss in 1986.
In their testimony, former Lucchese crime family captains Peter "Big Pete" Chiodo and Al D'Arco said Gigante was boss. So did Gravano, who testified that as Gambino underboss he met Gigante.
